topic: Flow on Android: lifecycle-safe collection & one-off events

questions.question: An Activity collects a location Flow with `lifecycleScope.launch { viewModel.locations.collect { render(it) } }` in `onCreate`. The user presses Home and the Activity is stopped. What happens to the collection?
options: It keeps running until the Activity is destroyed, so `render` runs while the UI is hidden
It is cancelled at `onStop` and restarted at `onStart`
It is paused at `onStop` and resumes from the same point at `onStart`
It is cancelled at `onPause`, because `lifecycleScope` follows the RESUMED state by default
questions.explanation: `lifecycleScope` is only cancelled at DESTROYED, so a plain `launch { collect }` keeps collecting in the background. That wastes resources (GPS, network) and can update Views while stopped. Being tied to STARTED needs `repeatOnLifecycle` or `flowWithLifecycle`.

questions.question: A ViewModel exposes navigation events through a `MutableSharedFlow(replay = 1)`. The first collector is cancelled (rotation) and a new one subscribes. What does this print?
options:
A: Navigate
B: Navigate
A: Navigate
B: Navigate

A: Navigate
B: null
questions.explanation: With `replay = 1` every new subscriber immediately gets the last value, so the re-created screen sees `Navigate` again and would navigate twice. That's why a replaying SharedFlow is a poor fit for one-off events.

questions.question: By default, `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` collects only while the lifecycle is at least `STARTED`.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Its `minActiveState` parameter defaults to `Lifecycle.State.STARTED`. Collection stops when the lifecycle drops below that and starts again when it comes back.

questions.question: A Fragment collects inside `viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { vm.uiState.collect { render(it) } } }`. The app goes to the background and then comes back. What happens to the block?
options: It is cancelled below STARTED and runs again from the start on returning to STARTED
It is suspended at `onStop` and picks up mid-collection at `onStart`
It runs once. Coming back to STARTED does nothing because `repeatOnLifecycle` has already returned
It keeps collecting, and only `render` calls are skipped while stopped
questions.explanation: `repeatOnLifecycle` launches the block in a new coroutine every time the lifecycle reaches the target state and cancels it when the lifecycle falls below. So collection really stops (not just pauses) and restarts from scratch, which is why a `StateFlow` (which hands the latest value to every new collector) pairs well with it.

questions.question: Why does a ViewModel usually declare `private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(UiState())` and `val uiState: StateFlow<UiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()`?
options: So the UI gets a read-only view and only the ViewModel can change the state
Because `MutableStateFlow` cannot be collected from a Fragment
Because `asStateFlow()` makes collection lifecycle-aware
Because `asStateFlow()` copies the current value so the UI and ViewModel never share state
questions.explanation: `asStateFlow()` wraps the mutable flow in a read-only `StateFlow`, so the UI can't set `value` or cast it back to `MutableStateFlow`. It doesn't add lifecycle awareness or copy anything: both sides still see the same live state.

questions.question: Which of these stop collecting a Flow when the screen goes to the background (below STARTED)? Select all that apply.
options: `lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { flow.collect { } } }`
`flow.flowWithLifecycle(lifecycle, Lifecycle.State.STARTED).onEach { }.launchIn(lifecycleScope)`
`val state by flow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` in a composable
`lifecycleScope.launch { flow.collect { } }` started in `onStart`
`lifecycleScope.launchWhenStarted { flow.collect { } }`
questions.explanation: `repeatOnLifecycle`, `flowWithLifecycle` and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` all cancel collection below STARTED. A plain `launch` lives until DESTROYED whichever callback started it (and launching it in every `onStart` stacks up duplicate collectors). The deprecated `launchWhenStarted` only suspends the coroutine, so the subscription and its upstream work stay alive.

questions.question: In Compose, plain `collectAsState()` stops collecting when the Activity is stopped, so it is just as lifecycle-safe as `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `collectAsState()` collects for as long as the composable is in the composition, and the composition stays alive while the Activity is stopped. It knows nothing about the lifecycle, which is why Android recommends `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.

questions.question: Inside `callbackFlow { }`, why does a listener such as `onLocationResult(result)` call `trySend(result)` instead of `send(result)`?
options: The listener isn't a suspend function, and `send` suspends while `trySend` doesn't
`send` closes the channel after the first element
`trySend` guarantees the element is delivered even when the buffer is full, while `send` may drop it
`send` only works with `Dispatchers.IO`
questions.explanation: `send` is a suspend function, so it can't be called from a normal callback. `trySend` returns a `ChannelResult` right away. It can fail when the buffer is full, so it does not guarantee delivery, and you can set a buffer policy (for example `buffer(Channel.CONFLATED)`) for fast producers.

questions.question: A fake location manager is wrapped with `callbackFlow`. What does this print?
options:
register
loc 1
loc 2
remove
done

register
loc 1
loc 2
done

register
loc 1
loc 2
done
remove

register
loc 1
loc 2
loc 3
remove
done
questions.explanation: Once `take(2)` has its two values it cancels the producer, which runs the `awaitClose` block (`remove`) before `collect` returns, so `remove` comes before `done`. The third value was buffered but is never delivered. Without `awaitClose` the listener would never be unregistered.

questions.question: When is `flow.flowWithLifecycle(lifecycle, Lifecycle.State.STARTED)` a better fit than writing `repeatOnLifecycle` yourself?
options: When you collect a single flow and want a chainable operator, e.g. before `launchIn`
When you collect several flows in parallel, because it shares one lifecycle observer between them
When you need the flow to keep collecting in the background but skip emissions while stopped
When the code runs outside any Activity or Fragment, because it doesn't need a `Lifecycle`
questions.explanation: `flowWithLifecycle` uses `repeatOnLifecycle` internally and only collects upstream while the lifecycle is at least the given state. It suits one flow. For several flows, use one `repeatOnLifecycle` block with a `launch` for each flow, rather than chaining the operator on each flow separately.

questions.question: A ViewModel uses `stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), UiState())` and the UI collects with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`. What is the 5-second timeout for?
options: Rotation resubscribes within 5 s so upstream keeps running; a longer background stay stops it
It delays the first emission by 5 s so the UI has time to subscribe
It caches the value for 5 s and then resets the StateFlow back to the initial value
It keeps upstream alive for 5 s after `viewModelScope` is cancelled, so pending results can still arrive
questions.explanation: `stopTimeoutMillis` waits that long after the last subscriber leaves before cancelling upstream. A config change resubscribes almost immediately, so the work isn't restarted, but a backgrounded app has no subscribers for more than 5 s and upstream stops. The value is kept by default (`replayExpirationMillis` is infinite).

questions.question: If a ViewModel uses `SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000)` but the Activity collects with a plain `lifecycleScope.launch { uiState.collect { } }`, the upstream still stops about 5 seconds after the user presses Home.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `WhileSubscribed` only reacts to subscribers actually leaving. A plain `lifecycleScope.launch` keeps its subscription until the Activity is destroyed, so the subscriber count never reaches zero and upstream keeps running. The saving only happens when the UI side is lifecycle-aware too.

questions.question: Navigation events go through `MutableSharedFlow<NavEvent>()` (replay = 0) and the screen collects them with `repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)`. A network call finishes and calls `events.emit(GoToDetails)` while the app is in the background. What happens?
options: The event is dropped: with no subscribers, nothing is stored
`emit` suspends until the screen returns to STARTED, then the event is delivered
The event is buffered and delivered when the screen resubscribes
`emit` throws `IllegalStateException` because there are no collectors
questions.explanation: A SharedFlow with `replay = 0` keeps nothing for future subscribers, and with zero subscribers `emit` does nothing and returns at once. The user comes back and the navigation never happens, which is the classic lost-event bug.

questions.question: Events are sent to a `Channel` before any screen is collecting. What does this print?
options:
screen1: Navigate
screen2: Toast

screen1: Navigate
screen2: Navigate
screen2: Toast
screen1: Navigate

screen1: Navigate
screen2: Toast
screen2: Navigate
questions.explanation: A Channel keeps elements until someone receives them, so nothing sent before collection is lost. Each element goes to exactly one receiver, so `Navigate` is gone once screen1 takes it. Stopping a `receiveAsFlow` collector doesn't close the channel (unlike `consumeAsFlow`), so screen2 gets the remaining `Toast`.

questions.question: A ViewModel exposes one-off events as `private val _events = Channel<UiEvent>(Channel.BUFFERED)` and `val events = _events.receiveAsFlow()`. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: Events sent while the screen is stopped are buffered and delivered when it collects again
If two collectors are active, each event goes to only one of them
After a rotation, the new Activity receives every past event again
Every active collector receives every event, as with a SharedFlow
questions.explanation: A buffered Channel holds events until they're received, so the background case works. Delivery is fan-out, though: one receiver per element, so it isn't for broadcasting to several observers. Elements are removed once received, so nothing is replayed after rotation.

questions.question: What does the official Android architecture guidance recommend for a one-off message like "Item saved" shown in a Snackbar?
options: Model it as state, e.g. `userMessage: String?` in `UiState`, cleared once the UI has shown it
Emit it on a `MutableSharedFlow(replay = 1)` so it survives rotation and is shown exactly once
Expose it as `LiveData<String>` and observe it with `observeForever`
Call the Snackbar directly from the ViewModel through a stored `View` reference
questions.explanation: Treating the event as part of the UI state means it survives config changes and lifecycle gaps, and the UI tells the ViewModel when it has been handled. A replaying SharedFlow would show it again on resubscribe, and holding a `View` in a ViewModel leaks the Activity. For example, the UI calls `userMessageShown()`, which sets `userMessage` back to `null`.

questions.question: If a `callbackFlow { }` block registers a listener and then simply returns without calling `awaitClose`, the flow completes normally when the block returns.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `callbackFlow` requires `awaitClose`. If the block returns while the channel is still open, collection fails with an `IllegalStateException` saying `awaitClose` should be used. `awaitClose` keeps the producer suspended while callbacks arrive and gives you a place to unregister the listener.

questions.question: Which statements about the LiveData and Flow interop extensions are true? Select all that apply.
options: `flow.asLiveData()` collects upstream only while the LiveData has active observers, and cancels after a timeout (5 s by default) once the last one goes away
`liveData.asFlow()` turns a LiveData into a cold Flow that emits its values while being collected
`flow.asLiveData()` starts collecting at creation and never stops until the ViewModel is cleared
`liveData.asFlow()` needs a `LifecycleOwner` parameter to observe the LiveData
questions.explanation: `asLiveData()` starts collecting when the LiveData becomes active and stops `timeoutInMs` (default 5000) after it becomes inactive, which works much like `WhileSubscribed(5000)`. `asFlow()` observes the LiveData with `observeForever` inside the flow, so it doesn't need a `LifecycleOwner`. The collector's lifecycle-aware collection handles that part.

questions.question: A composable reads `val state by vm.locationState.collectAsState()`, where `locationState` uses `stateIn(viewModelScope, WhileSubscribed(5000), ...)` over GPS updates. The user presses Home for 10 minutes. What happens?
options: GPS keeps running: the composition survives `onStop`, so `collectAsState` stays subscribed
GPS stops after 5 s, because Compose disposes the composition when the Activity is stopped
GPS stops immediately, because `collectAsState` uses the Activity's lifecycle by default
Collection continues, but `stateIn` drops the GPS values because `viewModelScope` is paused
questions.explanation: Compose doesn't dispose the composition at `onStop`, so `collectAsState` stays subscribed and the upstream keeps working. Switching to `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` unsubscribes below STARTED, and after 5 s `WhileSubscribed` cancels the GPS upstream.

questions.question: Even with a `Channel`, an event sent just as the screen goes to STOPPED is occasionally lost. Why does the guidance to collect events on `Dispatchers.Main.immediate` (for example `withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) { events.collect { } }` inside `repeatOnLifecycle`) help?
options: A dispatched resume leaves a gap where cancellation drops the element; `Main.immediate` resumes with no gap
`Main.immediate` makes `repeatOnLifecycle` ignore the STOPPED state until all buffered events are handled
`Main.immediate` turns the Channel into a replaying flow, so the event is delivered again after `onStart`
`Main.immediate` runs the collector on a background thread, so it is not cancelled with the lifecycle
questions.explanation: Cancellable suspensions in coroutines have a prompt cancellation guarantee: if the coroutine is cancelled before it actually resumes, it throws `CancellationException` and the already-taken element is lost. When the sender and collector are both on the main thread, `Main.immediate` (also the default for `viewModelScope` and `lifecycleScope`) avoids the re-dispatch and closes that window. It doesn't change cancellation or replay behaviour.
